an5.3:1.1: “Bhikkhus, possessing five qualities, a bhikkhu dwells in suffering in this very life—with distress, anguish, and fever—and with the breakup of the body, after death, a bad destination can be expected for him.
an5.3:1.3: Here, a bhikkhu is devoid of faith, morally shameless, morally reckless, lazy, and unwise.
an5.3:1.4: Possessing these five qualities, a bhikkhu dwells in suffering in this very life—with distress, anguish, and fever—and with the breakup of the body, after death, he can expect a bad destination.
an5.3:2.1: “Bhikkhus, possessing five other qualities, a bhikkhu dwells happily in this very life—without distress, anguish, and fever—and with the breakup of the body, after death, a good destination can be expected for him.
an5.3:2.3: Here, a bhikkhu is endowed with faith, has a sense of moral shame, has moral dread, and is energetic and wise.
an5.3:2.4: Possessing these five qualities, a bhikkhu dwells happily in this very life—without distress, anguish, and fever—and with the breakup of the body, after death, a good destination can be expected for him.”
